analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only or test-harness changes. No production source is modified.

- main.swift (head ~415-533): model-free checks for ClusterServiceAgentPlan. They assert a per-user launchd agent with no UserName/GroupName and an allowlisted environment, KeepAlive SuccessfulExit=false, and a label scoped to the install. They also cover idempotent install decisions and a status view that ignores a supervisor record from an earlier boot. These assertions reinforce the least-privilege posture and add no new attack surface.
- run.sh (lines 16-22): adds ClusterPairUpdateProgress.swift to the swiftc compile set. It is a local, checked-in source path, with no network fetch and no privilege change. The script runs the checks in an mktemp build dir cleaned by a trap.
- ClusterServiceUpdateTests.swift (new, 463 lines): the tests use temporary directories, shell-script fakes standing in for the service, unsigned fixtures (verifyCodeSignatures: false) and a loopback 127.0.0.1:9 coordinator URL. All of these are confined to test targets. The tests assert that a release failing its start check (non-zero exit, hang, or a different reported version) is never restarted into and is rolled back and quarantined. They also assert that an unhealthy candidate is rolled back after three failed starts and that a healthy candidate is promoted. These behaviors support T-043-style rollback and update integrity, but the production implementations (ClusterMemberSupervisor, ClusterPairUpdate, the SelfUpdater start check and the re-exec path) are not in the supplied evidence.

Remaining integration questions for the next pass:
1. Verify in production code that the start check runs the staged `darkbloom --version` only after the artifact's signature and hash verification. Executing a staged binary before verification would be a risk.
2. Verify that the update-request and progress files under the service directory are owner-only and that their contents are validated, so that a same-UID process cannot trigger a restart or spoof progress. T-059/T-060 cover a similar same-UID class for the add-on socket.
3. Verify that the pair-update flow cannot be used to drain a cluster without both Macs having the release.

No concrete security regression is identified from these test-only changes.
